answer: A bonding system forces every agent to lock collateral before acting: each identity posts a refundable stake, and any provably-linked duplicate gets both accounts slashed. An attacker cannot cheaply spin up thousands of identities because each costs real capital held hostage, and losing the whole lot on detection wipes out the profit of farming rewards. Honest agents withdraw their stake untouched, so identity spam becomes a losing trade: a sybil swarm that fleeces one haven of rewards destroys its own thread of funding, and the lotus that blooms from fraud is cut before payout.
